back: Some verbs work as both (e.g., 'She closed the door' vs 'The door closed') [14].
Verbs like answer, sing, study don't need objects if meaning is clear (e.g., 'She plays beautifully') [14].
Some verbs must have an adverb or prep phrase (e.g., 'The disease originated in Britain') [14].
Verbs like adhere to, belong to, deal with [14].
Verbs like associate with, base on, put on (e.g., 'Put the report on the floor') [14].
Verbs like hold, pronounce, believe (e.g., 'Hold the government responsible') [14].
Adding 'to be' or using a that-clause makes it less formal (e.g., 'believe the opposite to be true') [14].
